<reason>Both sides were sharp and format-compliant, and PRO deserves credit for an honest, clearly labelled concession rather than an evasion. But CON built and held the decisive comparative frame. CON's opening correctly predicted the fork ("distributive gesture dressed as conservation policy"), and PRO's rescue — priority inside a fixed conservation cap — walked straight into it: PRO then had to concede in [A4.1] that resident priority produces "no physical effect" on the fabric, and that inside a fixed cap the only funding route is surcharging the remaining outsiders, which CON credibly characterised as CON's own levy doing the work while pricing out the modest-income visitor. CON's eligibility dilemma (narrow = subsidise wealthy central-address holders; broad = millions of eligibles against a few thousand slots) forced PRO into a 10–20% quota, which CON immediately converted into the debate's most damaging line: four in five residents remain identically excluded, funded by shrinking the restoration budget — "it is a raffle." PRO's best live route, the access-versus-compensation distinction ("a levy is compensation for exclusion; priority is access"), is genuinely good and was never fully extinguished, and PRO's Q1 usefully pressed that CON's cap also displaces the once-in-a-lifetime visitor. CON answered that pressure directly with the "what does the exclusion buy" test, which reframed displacement comparatively rather than dodging it. On the whole exchange, CON gave the cleaner decision rule, absorbed PRO's strongest question, and made the cost-benefit of the motion easier to evaluate; PRO's residual benefit shrank to a small, unfunded lane for a minority.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [B4.3]–[B4.5]: taking PRO's own 10–20% quota figure and showing that four in five residents remain excluded exactly as under a plain cap, while the restoration budget shrinks to pay for the lucky lane — combining PRO's conceded "no physical effect" with PRO's own arithmetic to reduce the motion to a costly raffle.</best_rebuttal>
